newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden FinMin says EMU report findings "personal".
newsitem.headline: Sweden FinMin says EMU report findings "personal".

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Tuesday the findings of the Calmfors commission into the consequences of possible membership of the EMU single currency were based on the personal views of the members.

Asbrink said that the commission, whose findings were generally negative to Swedish participation in the single currency from the start in 1999, had provided a "very good, well written basis for the debate" on the EMU.

"At the same time, it is evident that the recommendations of the committee are ultimately based on personal assessments and values, and cannot be derived on scientific grounds alone, as the committee itself points out," Asbrink said in a statement.
He said the government would carefully study the comments and would present a bill in the autumn of 1997 regarding possible Swedish participation in the currency union.
The Calmfors report, published on Monday, said Sweden should adopt a softly-softly approach on EMU until the country's economic fundamentals were stronger.
However, it said Sweden should leave its options open to join at a later date.
